title: Italian tubular cast-on
subtitle: An invisible entry into 1x1 rib that mimics a knitted fold.
excerpt: The Italian tubular cast-on produces an edge that looks like a folded tube of stocking stitch. It is the standard opener for fine-gauge 1x1 rib and the go-to method wherever the lower edge must be completely invisible.
sourceNotes: Traditional Italian knitting technique documented in comparative stitch encyclopaedias. Method as described in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) under 'invisible cast-on' variants, adapted to the crochet-chain entry point.

glossaryTerms.definition: A two-row cast-on method that enters 1x1 rib with an invisible fold, giving the edge the appearance of a knitted tube. Requires working a set-up round in which knit and purl stitches are separated onto alternating loops.
A section of 1x1 rib preceded by a tubular cast-on (or followed by a tubular cast-off), giving both edges an invisible, seamless finish.

content.text: that has been folded under and sewn. The cast-on works by creating a provisional row of alternating knit and purl loops over two set-up rows, which are then worked into 1x1 rib. At the entry point, the fabric looks as if it simply began as a fold rather than a cast-on. Difficulty: advanced; the set-up rows are fiddly and require careful attention to which stitch is which.
Fingering-weight yarn (the method is most effective in fine yarn)
Waste yarn and crochet hook for the provisional entry

Using waste yarn and a crochet hook, chain the number of stitches you need to cast on plus a few extra. Pick up stitches from the chain bumps with your working needle and working yarn. This gives you a provisional row of live stitches.
Set-up row 1: (k1, bring yarn forward, sl1 purlwise, take yarn back) across. This separates the stitches into alternating knit and held-forward groups.
Set-up row 2: (sl1 purlwise with yarn in front, k1) across. On this row the stitches reverse roles.
Work 1x1 rib (k1, p1) normally from now on. The set-up rows have created the tubular entry.
When sufficient rib has been worked, unzip the provisional chain. The live stitches at the base will have folded under into the tubular structure.

The Italian tubular cast-on is the mark of a carefully finished garment. It appears at the lower edges of fitted jerseys, the cuffs of fine-gauge gloves, and wherever a beginner-friendly 'raw' cast-on edge would look out of place. Fine-yarn Shetland lace shawls occasionally use a tubular entry when the lower edge is to be grafted.

items.symptom: Set-up rows look like a normal knit row, not alternating
items.cause: Forgetting to bring yarn forward before slipping and take it back before knitting
items.fix: Work slowly on the first set-up row, placing a finger on the yarn to confirm its position before each stitch.

items.symptom: Rib does not form a clean fold at the entry
items.cause: Slip stitches worked purlwise with yarn on the wrong side
items.fix: The slipped stitches in row 1 need yarn in front; slipped stitches in row 2 need yarn behind. Reversing these locks the fold incorrectly.

items.cause: Not transferring released stitches to a needle quickly enough
items.fix: Keep a spare needle alongside while unzipping. Slide each released stitch onto it immediately before it can drop off.
